derivation: apparently from the same as G206 (ἄκρον);
def: a locust (as pointed, or as lighting on the top of vegetation)

occurrences.text: And the same John had his raiment of camel’s hair, and a leathern girdle about his loins; and his meat was locusts and wild honey.
And John was clothed with camel’s hair, and with a girdle of a skin about his loins; and he did eat locusts and wild honey;
And there came out of the smoke locusts upon the earth: and unto them was given power, as the scorpions of the earth have power.
And the shapes of the locusts were like unto horses prepared unto battle; and on their heads were as it were crowns like gold, and their faces were as the faces of men.

source: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890) and Concise Dictionaries (1894), public domain; JSON by Open Scriptures (CC BY-SA).
